final_recommendation: The room converged on a binding Protocol amendment framework: Congress votes Monday on explicit drafting instructions (joint inspections, 30-day automatic tariffs from joint panel finding, Mexico leads investigation), business signals investment support Tuesday, and Canada/Mexico enforce labor-only scope via auto-termination clauses. Ratification path clears contingent on this amendment.
minority_objections: Mexico initially resisted 'No Mexico Veto' headline framing as sovereignty infringement
Business lobby initially preferred ratification-as-is to avoid amendment uncertainty
key_conflicts: Headline wording ('No Mexico Veto' vs 'Mexico Leads Investigation') nearly derailed consensus in R3
Timing of Congressional vote (before vs after seeing final Protocol text) created trust deadlock in R4-R5
Ambiguity over whether memo constraints were binding or advisory threatened labor walkout in R6-R7
key_concessions: Mexico accepted joint panel determination of violations in exchange for leading investigation on Mexican soil
Labor accepted 'Mexico Leads Investigation' framing in exchange for automatic tariff trigger with zero discretion
Business accepted amendment uncertainty in exchange for binding enforcement that unlocks ratification
Congress committed to explicit drafting instructions binding memo language into Protocol text
red_lines: Canada: any drafting proposal touching dairy or Chapter 19 triggers immediate withdrawal (auto-termination clause)
Mexico: any drafting proposal touching dairy or Chapter 19 triggers immediate withdrawal
Labor: no 'joint panel discretion' or consultation loopholes in tariff trigger mechanism
Congress: votes conditional on memo constraints being binding on final Protocol text, not advisory
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Enforcement mechanism's operational details (30 days from joint panel finding vs Mexico notification) left partially ambiguous until R7
Business investment signaling delayed until Tuesday creates 48-hour window where labor could still walk
No discussion of what happens if Mexico's cabinet rejects the operational definition after Monday vote
downstream_risk_variables: Whether Mexico's cabinet actually signs off Monday that operational definition is binding
Whether drafting team respects memo constraints or proposes 'technically compliant' alternative language
Whether business statement Tuesday actually moves Congressional votes or just signals intent
Whether media framing shift from 'amendment talks' to 'enforcement credible, ratification clears' materializes
uncertainty_notes: Final Protocol text not yet drafted; room locked framework and constraints but actual language remains subject to Tuesday drafting session. Mexico's cabinet sign-off and business statement timing create 48-hour execution risk. Auto-termination clauses untested if drafters propose ambiguous language.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: R1 opening: 'I've got the votes to kill this thing right now' — ratification failure drove every subsequent move, including binding memo constraints and auto-termination clauses
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Labor's demand for 'inspectors, real penalties, automatic tariffs with zero discretion' shaped the entire amendment framework from R1 through R7; room converged on binding enforcement as ratification condition
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Business conditioned investment signaling on credible enforcement (R3-R4) and secured binding memo publication (R6), but accepted amendment uncertainty rather than driving the room's direction
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Canada's dairy red line and auto-termination clause (R7) were critical scope locks, but dairy itself was never seriously threatened — the room treated it as settled, not contested
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Mexico's insistence on 'leads investigation' vs 'no veto' framing (R3) and operational definition (R6-R7) shaped headline and memo language, but room accommodated this within joint panel framework
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Media framing ('Congress wins worker protections' vs 'talks stall') influenced headline negotiation (R3-R5) and narrative shift (R7), but did not drive the core enforcement mechanism design
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Room treated ratification as contingent on amendment from R1 onward; entire framework (binding memo, auto-termination clauses, Congressional vote timing) designed to make amendment credible and scope-limited

node: Node 2 - Domestic Ratification Pressure Room (initial USMCA package formed, before the 10 Dec 2019 Protocol of Amendment; information cutoff 2019-12-09)
